svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Bacteriophages are viruses that infect bacteria."], [1, "A phage attaches to the bacterium and injects its DNA."], [3.5, "Lytic cycle: the phage DNA is replicated and new phage parts are made."], [6.5, "New phages are assembled; the cell bursts and releases them."], [9.5, "Lysogenic cycle: the phage DNA joins the bacterial chromosome as a prophage."], [12.5, "The bacterium divides normally; every daughter cell carries the prophage."], [16, "A trigger such as UV light switches the prophage into the lytic cycle."]]
svg.title: Lytic and lysogenic cycles
svg.desc: A bacteriophage attaches and injects DNA; in the lytic cycle it replicates, assembles and lyses the cell; in the lysogenic cycle its DNA integrates as a prophage and is passed on at each division until induction.
svg.text: Red: phage DNA. Blue: bacterial chromosome.

g.data-info: The phage binds to specific receptors on the bacterial cell wall and injects its DNA; the protein coat stays outside.
The phage DNA takes over the cell: it is replicated, phage proteins are made, new phages are assembled and the cell bursts (lysis), releasing them.
The phage DNA joins the bacterial chromosome as a prophage and is copied every time the bacterium divides, without harming it.

g.text: cell divides: daughters inherit the prophage

g.data-info: A trigger such as UV light or stress makes the prophage leave the chromosome and enter the lytic cycle.

g.text: induction (e.g. UV light): prophage leaves the chromosome → lytic cycle
